title: Check generated variant registration and callers before reproducing a local anomaly
applies_when: A candidate comes from a partial window of generated, shape- or dtype-specialized kernel code, especially a low-level binding or reusable helper definition.
lesson: Retrieve the package registry and host dtype/shape dispatch before treating one physical kernel as the public API contract. Trace the suspected helper to an actual call, and substitute the specialized dimensions into padding/index arithmetic. A bf16-only binding can be correct for its registered key; a constant-false padding branch can be harmless when the dimension is already aligned; an unused helper does not establish an active ordering bug. These checks can refute the particular hypothesis without compiling its target environment.
avoid_when: Do not exclude all generated code or assume an unregistered shape is necessarily acceptable API behavior. Reopen with a supported logical key routed to the wrong variant, a reachable consumer of unwritten bytes, or a real helper call and compiler/runtime evidence. Static reachability and arithmetic are not native numerical correctness, performance or portability tests.

evidence.note: KERNELS maps architecture and logical dtype/shape/fold keys to physical generated modules. kernel_module_name rejects missing keys before loading a binding; the two inspected K8192 folded quantizers are bf16 keys, not shared fp16 implementations.

prepare_nvfp4_per_token_quantize derives the logical key from the actual input dtype. padded_sf_cols and the fixed K=8192 generated quantizer explain why a scale-column padding branch can be empty without missing required columns.

The suspect mbarrier_wait_relaxed_hint appears only as a definition in this complete translation unit, not a call or address reference. This is a scoped counterexample to inferring an active wait-ordering bug from the helper window alone.
